items.title: Studies test Enceladus microbes and plume-particle chemistry
items.content_html:
Two studies published in Science Advances examined whether a methane-producing Earth microorganism could remain active under laboratory conditions simulating Enceladus’s subsurface ocean, and how ocean material becomes ice grains in the moon’s plumes [scitechdaily.com#1][sciencedaily.com#1]. The microorganism survived, grew and produced methane in the simulated chemistry; the findings do not show that life exists on Enceladus [zmescience.com#1][newspaceeconomy.ca#1].

The second study found that ocean spray can sort and concentrate compounds into individual ice grains as it freezes and fragments. The process could also concentrate organic molecules and potential biosignatures [sciencedaily.com#1][astrobiology.com#1][scitechdaily.com#1].

items.title: "That's so AI" is the new insult, and it means bullshit
items.content_html:
Gen Alpha's slang makes it clear what kids think of so-called artificial intelligence. As reported by the Guardian, the most savage burn a young person can hurl at you is "That's AI" or "That's so AI."

The kids – gen Alpha – have noticed that certain qualities of AI-generated slop, such as the way it's superficially convincing but ultimately cheap and of dubious value, can be found in lots of other things: knock-off merchandise, exaggerated claims, excuses your parents make.

— Read the rest

items.title: What’s On Your To-Do List?
items.content_html:
I keep a list of things I want to do for KDO in Apple Notes, organized into four sections: small, medium, large, and longshots/obsolete. This note contains tweaks, bug fixes, code refactoring, new site features, roadmap items,1 infrastructure migrations, potential project ideas, vague prompts, and even things I don’t want to do but should maybe consider doing anyway at some point. I keep already-completed items on the list so progress can be gauged, noticed, and appreciated.

I was looking at the list today, and thought I’d share some of the items with you:

  • Reposting social posts (in comment threads) for members
  • Do a podcast
  • Publish posts to Instagram. (How?)
  • Implement site-wide search
  • Make newsletter daily?
  • Write a book based on kottke.org
  • Sell Blue Line Air Express t-shirts
  • Build a Substack competitor
  • Make a gift link search engine

Some of these are partly finished or would take very little to implement if I wanted. Some will never happen. Weirdly, some of the projects and site tweaks I most want to make aren’t even on my list. They live only in my head and I mull them over in the shower or while walking until they’re “done” enough to start working on. I guess maybe ideas don’t go on the list unless they’re not that urgent or interesting.

Do you have to-do lists for your creative projects? Care to share an item or two with the group?

  1. Insofar as KDO has a roadmap, which is somewhere between “not at all” and “a general direction into the murky haze of a possible future”. I play things by ear a lot. ↩
